verses.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea while Herod was king. Then some wise men from the east arrived in Jerusalem.
“Where is the child born to be King of the Jews?” they asked. “We saw his star rise in the east and have come to worship him.”
When King Herod heard this, he was shaken, and all Jerusalem was shaken with him.
He called together all the chief priests and the people’s teachers of the law and asked where the Messiah was supposed to be born.
They told him, “In Bethlehem of Judea. The prophet wrote:
“‘Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, you are definitely not the least among Judah’s leaders. A ruler will come from you, one who will shepherd my people Israel.’”
Then Herod secretly called the wise men and found out exactly when the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem, saying, “Go and search carefully for the child. When you find him, report back to me so I can go worship him too.”
After hearing the king, they set out. The star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.
They went into the house and saw the child with Mary, his mother. They bowed down and worshiped him, then opened their treasures and gave him gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they returned to their own country by another route.

After they left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. “Get up,” the angel said. “Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, because Herod is going to search for the child to kill him.”
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother during the night, and left for Egypt.
He stayed there until Herod died. This fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: “I called my son out of Egypt.”

When Herod realized the wise men had outsmarted him, he became furious. He sent men to kill every boy two years old and under in Bethlehem and the surrounding area, based on the time he had learned from the wise men.
Then what the prophet Jeremiah had spoken came true:
“A cry was heard in Ramah—grief, weeping, and deep mourning. Rachel was weeping for her children, and she refused to be comforted, because they were gone.”
After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in Egypt.
“Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to Israel,” the angel said, “because those who were trying to kill the child are dead.”
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and went to the land of Israel.
But when Joseph heard that Archelaus was ruling Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. After God warned him in a dream, he went instead to the region of Galilee.
He settled in a town called Nazareth. This fulfilled what the prophets had said: he would be called a Nazarene.
